note: Extracted from docs/DECISIONS.md §3 and docs/ATLAS.md §12.3. The benchmark register says what each test is; this says which to trust for which objective, and what never to report.

matrix.never: Pooled scores. Macro average only — a pooled number lets Hindi carry Santali.

trust: SWE-bench Verified with a named harness
matrix.never: Any number without the harness, scaffold version, turn limit and context window stated. Those four change the score more than the model does.
Preferred wording as evidence of correctness. Sounding Indian is not knowing India.
English-only safety testing. Safety alignment does not transfer across languages.

disciplines.title: Contamination is a build gate, not a check
disciplines.detail: 13-gram and MinHash against a registry that lives in CI and never enters the deployed bundle.
disciplines.precedent: LightningLM dropped a full 31.3B-token pool rather than down-weight it.

disciplines.title: One benchmark is never looked at during development
disciplines.detail: BhashaBench — domain-specific across Agriculture, Legal, Finance and Ayurveda, and unlikely to appear in web text.
disciplines.precedent: A benchmark you tune against stops being a measurement the first time you look at it.

disciplines.title: A private set, commissioned early
disciplines.detail: 3,000 items across 22 languages, written natively rather than translated.
disciplines.precedent: Every public Indic benchmark will be contaminated within 18 months.

disciplines.title: Every tier must have an instrument
disciplines.detail: If no benchmark would detect a tier's removal, cut the tier or add an instrument.
disciplines.precedent: You cannot defend a token budget you cannot measure.

split_policy.rule: Three-way split, declared before training, never revisited.
split_policy.detail: Train, validate and test are separated at the source level rather than the row level, so a paraphrase cannot land on both sides.
